issues.description: The problem specification and UML require a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void in SealSaloon, but the solution implements checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) and calls it from orderMeal as checkOrderReady(true). This changes the method signature and behavior (introducing an extra debug print) compared to the stated API, which can confuse students about the required method signature and produces undocumented output.
issues.suggestedFix: Adjust the solution to match the specified API: provide a public void checkOrderReady() (no parameters). If internal logging is desired, implement a private helper or an overloaded private method taking a boolean. Remove any undocumented debug prints from the public API and have orderMeal() call the no-arg checkOrderReady().

issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) specifies a public no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void on SealSaloon, but the solution implements checkOrderReady with a boolean parameter (public void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)). This signature mismatch means students comparing the specification to the provided solution will see the same conceptual operation named identically but with different method signatures, creating confusion about the expected API (and whether an overload or a different method is required).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the public API match the problem statement by adding or restoring a no-argument public void checkOrderReady() method. If internal logging control is needed, implement a private helper (e.g., private void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)) and have the public no-arg method call it, or provide an overloaded public checkOrderReady() that delegates to the boolean-taking implementation.
